0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 17 October 1961, after the draft finalized by the Optical and Mathematical Instruments Sectional Committee had been approved by the Engineering Division Council.
0.2 The surveyors compass is an instrument for determining the difference in direction between any horizontal line and a magnetic needle, the needle Magnetic compasses, though of limited pointing the magnetic north. accuracy, have the advantage of giving reading directly in terms of directions Prismatic compass, liquid, can or bearings referred to magnetic north. either be used independently or in conjunction with other angle measuring instruments in orienting a map or plane table and making a survey or traverse. 0.3

4.1 Sighting System - The sighting system shall consist of sighting vanes hinged diametrically opposne to each other on the outer case. The eyeing vane shall have a vertical line slot in the metal housing of the magnifying prism. The front or sighting vane shall have a fine vertical line marked on the lid window. 4.2 Magnet Assembly -The magnet assembly shall consist of a thin bar magnet fitted with a conical agate, sapphire, ruby or suitable hard metal beaiing at its centre. The north seeking end of the needle shall be marked with an arrow head. 4.3 Bearing Indicating System - The bearing indicating system shall consist of a graduated circular disc slightly larger in diameter than the length of the magnet, the graduations being on a translucent disc of motherof-pearl, mica or any other suitable material (see Fig. 2) and fastened to the magnet. 4.4 Damping-cum-Antiwear System - The liquid damping and antiwear device. The inside of housing coat of protective matt black paint. 4.5 Dip Adjusting Slide The dip adjusting 4 serves both as may be given a

slide shall consist of a small

4.6 Housing-The inner case shall have a sealing glass fixed to it to enable the graduations to be read and the whole of the magnetic assembly is rendered dustproof. There shall be a finger loop fixed to the casing. The outside of the casing shall be graduated as shown in Fig. 1. The bottom surface of the casing shall have an arrangement for fixing the compass on a suitable tripod. 4.7 Night Reading Device - The night reading luminised parts and a lubber line index (see Fig. 3). 4.8 Reading System - The reading prism attached to the outer case. 5. 5.1 Materials -All parts of the compass, shall be made of non-magnetic materials. 5.2 Magnetic magnet steel.

Needle - The magnetic needle shall be of good It shall be properly hardened and aged.

5.2.1 The magnetic moment of the needle shall be between 20 and 25 cgs units. Each pole of the magnetic needle shall have a flux of approximately 100 lines.

5.5 Pivot Mounting-The pivot shall be properly centred and fitted. Line of contact between pivot and mounting shall be continuously smooth and free from irregularities. 5.6 Liquid - Good quality kerosine, ethyl alcohol shall be used as the liquid. isopropyl alcohol or anhydrous

5.7 Prism - The prism shall he of good quality optical glass, colourless, free from bubbles, and shall be ground and brought to a high degree of polish on the reflecting and curved surfaces. 5.8 Sealing Glass, Lid Window and Index Glass - Polished glass, with parallel surfaces and with the edges ground truly circular, be used. 5.9 Dial - The dial, if made of mother-of-pearl, free from flaws, and shall be regularly formed daylight, or of good quality mica. 6 plate shall

IS : 1955- 1961 .6.7 Bearing Errors The total error in any magnetic bearmg, as read through the prism, shall not exceed f30 minutes and the direct reading of the dial against the lubber line on the sealing glass shall agree with the supplementary angle of the magnetic bearing within &2 degrees.

6.7.1 Each compass shall be tested against a magnetic meridian determined by a standard compass or magnetometer and the total error in any magnetic bearing as indicated by the north seeking end of the compass shall not exceed f30 minutes. 6.8 Time of Swing - Compasses shah be tested for time of swing at a temperature of 15�C. The magnetic needle shall be deflected 90" from the magnetic meridian as viewed through the prism and kept there for an interval of 30 seconds in order to allow the compass liquid to settle; when released, the suspension unit shall return to rest in not less than 9 seconds nor more than 12 seconds.
